subject: Slimline tier & feature unbundle request — staffing + pricing options
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@straithealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@straithealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We ran the usage numbers across our pilot and it looks like two of the premium features (cross-region replication and long-term KV retention) are significantly underutilized for the next 6–9 months.

Before we sign, can we explore a "slimline" option that:
- removes cross-region replication for the first year,
- reduces KV retention to 30 days (from 365),
- keeps the core model serving capacity at the committed level (32 concurrent GPUs), and
- preserves the analytics/Trace logs add-on.

Also: what does a single-year term with a modest seat discount look like vs. a 3-year commit? We have a procurement window at the end of next week.

Would appreciate a simple SKU/pricing sheet and any impact notes on latency/SLOs we should expect.

—Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Platform Engineering, StraitHealth
emma.jones@straithealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@straithealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the note and for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can create a "slimline" variant and we can model 1yr vs 3yr economics. Longer details below plus I've attached a quick pricing sheet (StraitHealth_pricing_v3.pdf) and a draft MAP (MAP_STRAITHEALTH.xlsx).

High-level impacts:
- Cross-region replication: removing this removes automatic failover and geo-read locality. Latency for intra-US clients is unchanged; global failover RTO will be longer (manual remediation). No model degradation.
- KV retention from 365 -> 30 days: reduces storage + hotspot cache write amplification; token cost unchanged but cold-starts for older conversations may require rewarm (slight increase in tail latency on rarely accessed sessions).
- Committed serving capacity: leaving 32 GPUs as-is preserves throughput and per-token unit pricing in the sheet.

Pricing options included in the sheet:
1) 12-month term, slimline: 8% list discount + 6% seat credit applied to monthly committed capacity.
2) 36-month term, slimline: 14% list discount + 12% seat credit.
3) 12-month with limited rollback clause (one-time re-enable of cross-region for up to 2 weeks): +3% fee for the option.

Next steps I recommend:
- You review the attached MAP and mark which option you prefer.
- If 12-month looks best, I can loop Ben (pricing lead) to see if we can extend a one-time procurement discount to satisfy finance.

Attaching: StraitHealth_pricing_v3.pdf (pricing table + delta rows) and MAP_STRAITHEALTH.xlsx (mutual action plan).

If helpful, we can do a 20–30 minute call today to walk the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior GTM — Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@straithealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Emma —

Quick note from pricing: the numbers Marissa shared are in-range. Two tactical suggestions that often help customers who want optionality without full feature removal:

1) Feature toggle with phased billing: we can disable cross-region replication immediately but keep the product SKU available as a charged option at a lower, "standby" price. If you re-enable within the first 12 months we credit you back a prorated portion.

2) KV retention tiers: instead of 30 days flat we offer a 3-tier model (30/90/365) with automated migration costs spelled out. That gives you a safe baseline and a simple upgrade path.

If StraitHealth can commit on a 12-month P0 (core capacity) we can add a one-time procurement credit of 4% off the invoice to help align your FY cadence. That would stack with the 8% list discount Marissa noted (capped per deal).

Happy to jump on a call if you want to run through final invoice examples.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@straithealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Jones <emma.jones@straithealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Thanks Marissa / Ben —

Quick clarifying Qs from procurement/security before we finalize: 
1) If we opt into the phased billing toggle for cross-region, do you provide any SLA around restore time if we need to re-enable?
2) For the 4% procurement credit, are there any internal approvals we should be aware of or is this conditional on signature within 5 business days?

Also: can you provide a single-line SKU export we can drop into our procurement system (vendor catalog requires line items)? We need unit prices, quantity, term, and a short description.

If you can send the SKU export and the updated MAP with those clarifications we can move to signature.

—Aamir
Aamir Khan
Senior Manager, IT Procurement, StraitHealth

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@straithealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Hi Aamir —

Answers inline:
1) Phased billing toggle & SLA: the toggle itself is a billing/feature flag; we don't provide an automated failover SLA when cross-region is disabled. If you re-enable, re-provisioning completes within 2–6 hours for standard regions and up to 24 hours if capacity needs to be allocated in an alternate region. For customers needing guaranteed multi-region failover we recommend keeping the replication SKU live.

2) 4% procurement credit: this is conditional on countersignature within 7 business days from final SOW execution. No additional internal approvals beyond standard finance signoff; we'll include the credit line in the DocuSign-ready contract.

3) SKU export: attached below is a compact export block you can paste into your procurement system (also added to the MAP spreadsheet):

SKU|Description|UnitPrice|Qty|Term
RID-COMM-32|Committed serving (32 GPUs) - monthly equivalent|$42,500|12|12m
RID-KV-30|KV retention 30d - per GB month|$0.18|2500|12m
RID-TRACE|Analytics & Trace logs - annual|$12,000|1|12m
RID-REPL-OPT|Cross-region replication (standby option)|$3,500|12|12m
RID-SUPPORT-PREM|Premium SLA (4hr support) - annual|$18,000|1|12m

I'll also flag the DocuSign envelope with the credit lines once you confirm the option.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@straithealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@straithealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating our package — can we slim the plan?

Marissa / Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the SKU export — that's exactly what procurement needs. We reviewed the MAP and prefer:
- 12-month slimline option,
- KV tier at 30 days with option to upgrade to 90 within 60 days,
- cross-region replication disabled with the standby option (we accept the 2–6 hour reprovision window), and
- we accept the 4% procurement credit conditional on signature in 7 business days.

Please send the DocuSign package (we need the unit prices in the contract lines). If you can include the standby pricing and the credit line explicitly that will help legal sign-off.

Targeting signature by EOD next Thursday.

Thanks —
Emma
Head of Platform Engineering, StraitHealth
emma.jones@straithealth.com
